invalidation: Retire if the BOTH-directions configuration drops below profit factor 1.0 over 40 out-of-sample trades, or if it stops beating an always-long and always-short control on the same exit geometry. Do not judge the long and short legs separately: each fails alone and the pair is the strategy.
name: Donchian Breakout Trail

provenance.evidence_note: Walk-forward across the 16 declared symbols at 4h: median out-of-sample win rate 38.85%, median PF 1.447, 487 out-of-sample trades. The win rate is the envelope the live record is judged against — at 38.85% a run of three losses is ordinary and must not read as breakage.
provenance.note: Found by testing what every earlier sweep could not express. Prior geometry sweeps used trail kind none with a fixed RR target and a short hold cap, which amputates the fat right tail this style lives on. With no target, a 4 ATR trailing stop and a long hold, median PF is 1.22 across five sequential yearly windows (4/5 profitable), while always-long and always-short controls on identical geometry fail in 0/5. Long alone wins 2/5 and short alone 3/5: the directions are anti-correlated across regimes and only the pair works.
provenance.universe_note: 16 crypto perps. XAU and XAG were in the first symbol list and contributed NOTHING: they are recent listings with 1589 and 1427 4h bars, and the mechanism fires only 20 trades on each across the whole period — under 5 per fold, so every window scored nan and was silently dropped from the medians. The 18-symbol and 16-symbol results are identical to two decimals. They are also untradeable on Binance Demo, which lists crypto perps only. Re-test them once they carry a few years of history.

thesis: A break of a multi-week range persists because risk is repriced slowly: systematic participants scale in over days and trapped counter-positions cover into the move, so the tail of a breakout is fatter than its body. A trailing stop harvests that tail, while a fixed target amputates it and turns a positive-expectancy mechanism into a losing one.
